# University of the Andes (Colombia) Summary
The University of the Andes (Universidad de los Andes, Uniandes) was founded in 1948 by Mario Laserna Pinzón as Colombia’s first nonsectarian and non-politically affiliated university, aiming to train professionals and leaders for national development. Modeled after U.S. universities, Uniandes offers a critical, ethical, and pluralistic education, maintaining political neutrality and fostering technical and liberal knowledge. Classes began in 1949, and early innovations included exchange partnerships that enabled students to finish degrees abroad. The institution has actively recruited foreign faculty and established a reputation for international engagement and academic excellence.
Administratively, Uniandes operates as a private, nonprofit corporation with governance shared between the Board of Trustees, Board of Directors, Rector, and Academic Council. It features 14 academic units, including 10 faculties, and supports interdisciplinary study by allowing students to design curricular paths. The faculty is highly qualified, with 70% holding PhDs from leading global universities. The university’s student body is predominantly high-achieving, with 30% from outside Bogotá. Uniandes maintains a modern urban campus in Bogotá’s historical center, comprising renovated buildings and new facilities, extensive libraries with over 445,000 volumes, robust computing resources, sports centers, and health services. It hosts academic exchange programs with 119 universities in 34 countries and is recognized for notable alumni in government, science, the arts, and business. The university mascot is a goat named Seneca, symbolizing the institution’s inclusive culture.
